content:
Quick answer: Long-chain omega-3 fats (EPA and DHA) from oily fish — and algae oils if you avoid fish — are the food sources most often discussed for inflammatory joint conditions in UK guidance. Aim for at least one oily-fish portion a week as a food-first habit; higher intakes sometimes used in research are a clinician or pharmacist conversation, not a DIY megadose. Plant ALA (flax, walnuts, chia) helps overall diet quality but converts to EPA/DHA inefficiently. Omega-3 foods support an anti-inflammatory pattern — they do not rebuild cartilage or replace NHS care.

People search for omega-3 when joints ache and supplement aisles shout promises. This guide stays food-first for UK kitchens, with honest limits. Pair it with the diet hub, the pain-relief guide, and — if you are still orienting after diagnosis — newly diagnosed. Capsule comparisons live on the supplements hub and knee supplements guide.

Why omega-3s show up in arthritis conversations

EPA and DHA influence inflammatory signalling. That is why oily fish appear in Mediterranean-style patterns discussed for rheumatoid arthritis and general joint health. Effects are usually modest and gradual. They are not a cure, and response varies person to person.

Best food sources in a UK shopping basket

  • Oily fish: salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring, trout, anchovies — fresh, frozen or tinned in spring water/oil.
  • Budget wins: tinned sardines or mackerel on toast; frozen salmon portions.
  • Algae-based foods/oils: useful if you are vegetarian or vegan and want EPA/DHA without fish.
  • ALA plants: ground flaxseed, chia, walnuts — valuable, but not a like-for-like swap for oily fish EPA/DHA.

UK healthy-eating advice commonly includes at least one oily-fish portion weekly for the general population. People with inflammatory arthritis sometimes discuss higher intakes with their team; do not self-prescribe high-dose oils if you take anticoagulants, have bleeding risks, or have upcoming surgery.

Practical weekly pattern (not a prescription)

  • Plan two fish meals if you eat fish — make one oily.
  • Keep tinned fish in the cupboard for flare weeks when cooking is hard.
  • Cook with olive oil as your default fat; add walnuts or ground flax to porridge or yoghurt.
  • If you try a supplement, choose a clear EPA+DHA label, check interactions at a pharmacy, and set a review date.

What omega-3 foods will not do

They will not reverse structural osteoarthritis, replace DMARDs for inflammatory arthritis, or outperform a paced exercise plan. Movement and weight advice where relevant still sit at the centre of NICE-aligned osteoarthritis care. If money or mobility is the main stressor, use the Benefits & PIP hub alongside food changes.

Quick questions

Is cod an oily fish? White fish such as cod are healthy protein but low in EPA/DHA compared with mackerel or sardines.

Can I rely on flaxseed alone? ALA conversion is limited. If you avoid fish, discuss algae-based EPA/DHA with a clinician or dietitian.

How soon might I notice anything? Dietary patterns are judged over weeks to months. Worsening hot swollen joints need clinical review sooner.
